text.p: Swiss shares fell for the third day in a row to end lower after a nervous session dominated by professionals.
Dealers said most investors were sidelined ahead of Friday's U.S. employment data.
Sentiment was also marred by easing CONF futures and the U.S. dollar as well as an overnight fall on Wall Street and a slump in German shares, they said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index fell 24.7 points, or 0.55 percent, to 4,464.0 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index was down 17.67 points, or 0.62 percent, to 2,833.92.
Dealers said the jerky moves in index heavyweights Roche and UBS were symptomatic of the market as a whole.

Most-active Roche certificates ended off five francs at 11,720 after moving between 11,705 and 11,950. UBS bearers slid six francs to 1,239 after being temporarily quoted more than one percent higher.
Novartis slipped 15 francs to 1,721, while Ciba gained 2.50 to close at 116.
CS Group fell 3.75 francs to 159.50. Insurer Winterthur bucked the trend in financials, advancing seven francs to 998.
Watchmaker SMH rebounded from recent weakness. Its bearer shares climbed 15 francs to 785. ABB and Alusuisse sank 14 francs to 1,667 and 11 francs to 1,167, respectively.
Swissair, which is due to release 1996 figures on Friday, was down 18 francs to 1,230.
